clue.text: Appeal from lover to flirt heartlessly

indicators.note: a word without its heart loses its middle letter

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer
TOY (to flirt, as in toy with) without its middle O

explanation.surface: Someone calls on a sweetheart to stop flirting so coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: Appeal here is the noun for attractiveness, not a plea, which is what the surface makes it look like.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty is a plain synonym for appeal in its noun sense, the quality that attracts.

clue.text: One that covers up clean habit

parts.note: to bath someone is to clean them
a habit is a monk's or nun's robe

explanation.surface: Something that hides a tidy routine, or a cover-up for a good habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit is the monk's garment, not a routine; read that way the wordplay itself is almost a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: this garment's job is covering you up after washing.

clue.text: African plant, a strange bulbous one

parts.note: used as it stands
rum is British slang for odd or strange
a lily grows from a bulb

explanation.surface: A botanist describes an odd, swollen plant found in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Strange looks like an anagram signal, but here it means RUM, an old British word for peculiar, as in a rum do.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: this lily grows wild in southern Africa.

clue.text: Strip and review private patient's inside

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the letters read backwards
the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: privatE PATient

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to undress a private patient and examine their insides.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes strip a verb, but the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a roll of this sticky stuff unwinds as one long narrow strip.

indicators.note: one piece goes before the other in the answer

parts.note: a mat is a thick pad, and also a thick tangle of hair
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing a heavy pad on their head, perhaps a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'thick pad' twice on purpose: the whole phrase defines, and its last two words also give MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the thing you sleep on is a big slab of padding.

parts.note: read as filling in paperwork, and meant as a way of phrasing a question
read as a personal computer, and meant as a police constable to whom the question goes

explanation.surface: An instruction to fill in a form enquiring about a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer and form like paperwork; in fact PC is a police constable and the clue describes the kind of enquiry you put to one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the old British advice for any question in the street was to put it to the nearest constable.

clue.text: System of government that Cicero condemned

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase, the answer an adjective describing such a system

indicators.note: what is condemned is torn down, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A history lesson: the Roman orator Cicero denounced a form of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Cicero really did attack tyrannies, so the surface reads as fact; the orator is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: rule by priests in the name of a god is the system this word describes.

parts.note: read as a fixture scheduled at the other side's ground, and meant as a plan to run off
read as a game, and meant as a marriage

explanation.surface: A fixture has been scheduled at the other team's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Away match sounds like football; the match is a marriage, arranged away from home without the families.
explanation.definitionFit: The couple fixed their own marriage, or match, and ran away from home to hold it.

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so we take the sound of the word

parts.note: sighting something is observing it

explanation.surface: A commentator watches a televised round of golf, studying the putts.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting is the golf stroke in the surface but means placing here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting a building somewhere means choosing its site.

definitions.meaning: to beat or outdo, as when a higher card is played
the surname of a US head of state

explanation.surface: A description of the most senior head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is a verb here, not an adjective describing the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to outdo someone at cards or anything else, and the surname of a US head of state.

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A man who has not changed his shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man. The surface says the man has not changed; the letters of 'a bloke not' are what change.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a short boot reaching just past the ankle is one kind of footwear.

clue.text: Unfortunately, men take up arms in fairground

indicators.note: things going badly out of order suggests the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A news report of men arming themselves and fighting at a funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Take up arms suggests a battle, which makes the cheerful answer hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a site full of rides and sideshows is a fairground.

clue.text: A bit funny old Penny's missing list

indicators.note: the named letter is left out

parts.note: droll means mildly amusing
d was the symbol for an old British penny, before 1971

explanation.surface: Someone finds it amusing that an old friend called Penny is not on the list.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; with 'old' it is the pre-decimal British penny, written d.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the register of names called out at school is a list.

indicators.note: the word loses the letter it originally started with

parts.note: well-upholstered is a jokey way of saying fat; drop the first letter

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture that was not padded to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Well-upholstered sounds like a sofa, but it is humorous slang for a plump person.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a chunk of coal or sugar is a small block.

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
to prop something is to lean it against a support

explanation.surface: A stage prop used in a college play is immaculate.
explanation.walkthrough: Prop reads as a theatre object, but it is the verb: to prop a ladder against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something without a single spot of dirt is free of dirt entirely.

clue.text: Something to avoid — ice tea Firenze produces

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into something new

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A tourist warns that the iced tea made in Florence is best avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits 'ice tea' so that ice ends the definition and tea starts the fodder. Firenze is the Italian name for Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by purpose: the liquid in car radiators exists to stop ice forming.

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: BAT, a stick, loses its last letter
a lance is a knight's spear

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a small stick against a proper weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is the object here, a cricket or baseball bat, not the verb meaning to adhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to weigh two options against each other is to compare them.

definitions.meaning: the small pellets fired from a shotgun are made of a heavy metal
to go ahead and show the way

explanation.walkthrough: Shot looks like an attempt or a photograph; here it is the metal the pellets are cast from.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the metal that shotgun pellets are cast from, and the verb for going first to show the way.

clue.text: Type of revitalising product that comes from film concern

parts.note: a skin is a thin film, as on custard
care means concern or worry

explanation.surface: An advert for a rejuvenating cream made by a movie company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film concern' reads as one unit, a movie studio; the seam falls between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: creams sold to revive the complexion belong to this category of product.

definitions.meaning: the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.surface: A woman who has been proposed to and is now engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as one engagement; they are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a planned course of action, and the old-fashioned word for one's fiancé or fiancée.

indicators.note: turned about, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to edit a text is to change it

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of changing direction.
explanation.walkthrough: About to reads as 'on the point of', but about is the reversal signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the general drift of events, as in the tide of history, is their course.

explanation.walkthrough: Layer reads as a stratum, but it is something that lays.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for cowardly, and a hen as a bird kept for its eggs.

parts.note: flying can mean going very fast
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Birds migrating south for the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Flying south is what these birds actually do in autumn, so the whole clue reads as a nature note.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: these fast summer migrants are one kind of bird.

indicators.note: half of the word's heart, the double L in the middle, is removed

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas; drop one of its central Ls

explanation.surface: Someone took a slice of German cake without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-heartedly usually means without enthusiasm; here the heart of STOLLEN is LL, and half of it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something pinched without permission has been taken.

indicators.note: the phrase pens, or encloses, the answer

parts.note: coW AT ERgonomic

explanation.surface: A manatee, the sea cow, is kept in well-designed enclosures.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea cow reads as one animal, the manatee, but sea alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an ocean is the largest body of this liquid.

clue.text: Tiny one with energy to produce spell

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the sick boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A small child with plenty of energy casts a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell sounds like magic or spelling; it is a period, as in a spell of fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a spell of rain is a stretch or period.

indicators.note: the word returns the way it came, reading backwards

parts.note: Etna is the active volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: An Italian who smokes returned before something else happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoker looks like a person with a cigarette; it is a volcano that smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin prefix meaning earlier, as in antenatal, which crosswords treat as a word.

clue.text: Clever wire top of champagne is missing

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

parts.note: a cable is a wire

indicators.note: that letter is taken away

parts.note: first letter of champagne, removed from the wire

explanation.surface: A clever gadget: a wire cage over a champagne cork, its top gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wire cage round a champagne cork fits the surface, but wire here just means cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a capable, skilled person is described as clever.

clue.text: Lands a few jumps — promising situation that comes to nothing

definitions.text: promising situation that comes to nothing

indicators.note: the letters leap about into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A showjumper clears a few fences, which looks promising until it all goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Lands and jumps paint a sporting scene; lands is not a verb here but part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a first glimmer of light that turns out not to be sunrise, used of hopes that fade.

indicators.note: the outer word gathers the other inside it

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A poet gathers together an unremarkable committee.
explanation.walkthrough: Panel is a group of people, like a set of directors, though a wooden panel also works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a group of directors or examiners sitting together is a panel.

clue.text: Spooner's finished it, creating platforms at sea

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

parts.note: finished = done, which takes its S from the next word
it = sex, as in sex appeal, which takes its D from done

explanation.surface: A cheeky one-liner about someone finishing it off while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a crossword convention for sex or sex appeal; swapping the opening sounds of 'done sex' is the cheeky joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the open top decks of a cruise ship are raised platforms at sea.

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, from definitive
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A sports report says a match ended superbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Contest is a noun in the surface but a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: to fight a lawsuit rather than concede it is to contest the claim.
